content:
Sam: Heads up — we're seeing a growing cluster of small leftover GPU slots in us-west1 that are causing 20-35% of training pods to stay Pending. Not classic fragmentation; looks like a 'microshard' pattern where lots of tiny free slot leftovers prevent new 8-GPU jobs from packing.
Priya: ack. Do we have a metric to quantify?
Sam: grafana panel: gpu_free_slot_histogram shows a spike at <1 GPU bins. also metric: gpu_fragmentation_ratio=0.38 -> up from 0.12 this morning.
Carlos: any recent changes to node labels/taints? network-affinity or AZ pinning?
Sam: nothing deliberate. saw an autoscaler bump yesterday that created many small-instance nodes (g4dn.xsmall-ish) for short-lived batch tests. they left behind 0.5-2 GPU holes across many nodes.
Priya: that explains it. two options: 1) run a consolidation pass (evict tiny pods, drain nodes, reprovision to larger instances) or 2) enable opportunistic coalesce in the scheduler to relax strict GPU contiguity. short-term I'm +1 for consolidation.
Carlos: agree. but evicting can trigger retries and IO load. we should OOO a low-risk window and target nodes with >=75% fragmented free fraction.
orch-bot: [alert] cluster/us-west1/gpu-pool: available_gpus=124 total_gpus=420 fragmented_slots=162 (38%).
Sam: plan proposal: 1) run a dry-run probe script to list candidate nodes (no evictions) 2) during 23:00-01:00 UTC run a staged drain: cordon -> graceful-evict for low-priority pods -> delete ephemeral nodes -> reprovision with fewer larger instances. 3) keep a 15% burst pool so production doesn't starve.
Priya: please paste the probe command, I'll review before we run. also add a rollback path.
Carlos: I'll take the dry-run and the first two drains. Sam you own reprovision / infra request.
Sam: probe command (dry-run):
```
# list nodes where free_gpu_fraction < 0.25 but free_gpu_count > 0 and many small holes
python tools/gpu_probe.py --region us-west1 --min-free-frac 0.01 --max-contiguous 2 --dry-run
```
Priya: nice. can the probe output a csv? makes review easier.
Sam: it does. I'll share S3 link after running.
Carlos: for the drain we should use: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120` and orchestrate at most 5 nodes concurrently. add a pre-check to ensure node isn't hosting long-running GPU training with >10% progress.
Priya: add a cheap canary: pick 2 nodes with the worst fragmentation and run through the full path, verify pods reschedule cleanly and latency/cost signals stable.
Sam: agreed. I'll schedule the canary at 23:00 UTC. Carlos, start the dry-run in 10m and paste the csv.
Carlos: starting dry-run now. will post results in this thread.
Sam: also flagging cost note — if we reprovision to larger instances we increase spend per-node but should reduce idle fragmented capacity and lower per-token GPU charge. I'll update the cost estimate once we know target shapes.
orch-bot: [info] action_required: dry-run completed. output: s3://redwood-gpu-probe/us-west1/microshard-dryrun-1719009999.csv
Carlos: uploaded CSV. top hit nodes: node-az1-142 (fragmented_slots=6, free_total=3.5 GPUs), node-az2-079 (frag=5, free_total=2 GPUs), node-az1-211 (frag=8, free_total=4 GPUs).
Priya: looks consistent. Carlos pls pick node-az1-142 and node-az2-079 for canary drains. Sam, if reprovision request needs approval ping infra-costs.
Sam: will do. I'll also open an autoscaler rule ticket to avoid future small-instance churn.
Carlos: initiating canary drain for node-az1-142 in 5m. will post logs.
Sam: thanks — please annotate any unexpected evictions here (OOMs, long reschedules).
Carlos: canary done, one small job retried successfully, one ephemeral spot pod terminated (expected). total reschedule time sub-2m for training controller.
Priya: good signal. I vote proceed with staged consolidation overnight. post your concurrency plan and I'll approve.
Sam: concurrency: 5 nodes at once, pause 10m between waves, max 2 waves per AZ. rollback: reprovision new nodes -> wait 10m health -> if >5% of high-priority pods Pending then stop and revert by recreating old instance types.
Priya: approved. Carlos: proceed when ready.
Carlos: starting wave 1 now. will update on progress.
Sam: thanks team. follow-up: after wave 1 fragmentation ratio dropped to 0.21. will continue monitoring.
Priya: nice improvement. schedule a follow-up retro tomorrow to discuss autoscaler shaping and scheduler heuristics to prevent microshard buildup. :calendar:
